slices.description: The WRITE half of the WP supply path — where an allocate op would be minted and where e_t_s enters the board. Lock 1 (no verb writes an allocate op; requires_proposed_actor is an orphan-read precondition) and Lock 2 (e_t_s hardcoded 0.0 at the CLI writers; plan.priority_ranks excludes e_t_s<=0) live here. These two are SERIAL: fixing either alone changes nothing measurable. Determine the minimal durable writer design that satisfies both in ONE increment, and whether it belongs in the daemon engine or the CLI surface.

The READ half and the elimination gates — how ops are folded into board state, how capability/host matching eliminates candidates, and why the allocator receives an EMPTY input set (measured: ready=0, blocked=[], 0 allocate ops ever, against ~990 fleet-wide). Includes the state-neutral claim path, the fail-closed exact (kind,name) capability match that silently eliminates a lane declaring bk-* against a buildkit-* requirement, and host folding in resolve_host. NOTE: confirm.py is ABSENT from develop - the addressing reader bc203794 exists only on the untagged branch feat/scheduler-transition-verb-20260816, so this slice must reason about a stranded fix, not a merged one.

The cross-repo / cross-host deployment substrate the superset must ride on, and its measured defects. Per-machine install registry and per-target store dirs; target-id derived as sha1 of a CASE-VARYING resolved path (deploy recorded fb9d55f94f8b, marathon resolves 85444bd44ab0 - same repo, one segment's case apart, and the deploy record names an OS user whose home does not exist here); per-version venvs under the deploy home vs a shared user-site install; and the reproduced Windows failure where a concurrent buildkit*.exe makes any pip install half-uninstall and destroy the toolchain for EVERY lane. Determine how a superset fix is installed and enabled on all repos on this host and then on other hosts WITHOUT this class of destruction.

The CONSUMER half: what a delivered WP must bind to on arrival, and why intake fails even when supply exists. Roadmap<->pipeline reconcile joins feature_id by STRING EQUALITY, reads only status='complete', and on no match executes 'continue' - silently untouched, then reported in-sync. Measured identity breakage: the 078 roadmap slug != its spec directory (the spec records this as instance 13, and 069 has the same gap), AND specs/ carries three duplicate feature numbers (036, 050, 064) plus a 065 slug divergence. Determine the intake contract a superset must satisfy so a supplied WP reaches marathon/specify rather than vanishing at the join.
